paper_metadata.title: A comparative study of two C-containing high-entropy alloys Al0.3CrFeNi2 and Al0.3CoCrFeNi

evidence.quote: Two Al0.3CoCrFeNi and Al0.3CrFeNi2 high-entropy alloys (HEAs) containing ~0.07% carbon were designed to explore the feasibility of replacing expensive Co with Ni.
Two Al0.3CoCrFeNi and Al0.3CrFeNi2 high-entropy alloys (HEAs) containing ~0.07% carbon were designed to explore the feasibility of replacing expensive Co with Ni.

XRD diffraction indicates that the two HEAs in the solid solution state are single FCC structure (γ) (Co–S1000 and Ni2–S1000 in Fig. 2).
Two weak diffraction peaks, identified as the γ′-Ni3Al phase (L12 structure), were detected after aging at 550 ◦C (Co-A550 and Ni2-A550 in Fig. 2).
After aging at 550 ◦C, uniformly distributed L12 nano-particles are found in the matrix. The L12 showed a cube-cube orientation relationship with the matrix.
There is little coarsening of the L12 phase, whose size is 19.8 ± 1.4 nm (Fig. 4 (e)).

When the aging temperature was increased to 700 ◦C, the rod-shaped B2 phase in addition to L12 precipitation occurred in the matrix (Fig. 4 (d)). ... The length of the rod-shaped B2 phase is 71.3 ± 21 nm, according to Fig. 4 (d ~ f).
When aged at 900 ◦C, only the rod-shaped B2 phase can be found in the matrix without the L12 phase (Fig. 4 (g ~ i)).
Numerous precipitated phases with a size of ~100 nm appeared near the grain boundary after aging at 700 ◦C in Al0.3CrFeNi2 (Fig. 8 (a)).
Similar to the microstructure of Co-A550 in Fig. 4 (a ~ c), nanoscale L12 particles (6 ± 0.9 nm) are found to embed in the matrix.

Besides, both M23C6 and L12 particles agglomerate at grain boundary (Fig. 6 (d, f, h)). The M23C6 phase is verified by both the SAD pattern in Fig. 6 (j) and the enrichment of Cr and C in Fig. 6 (f) and (i).
Fig. 7 displays that the size of L12 precipitation in the matrix grew to 21.5 ± 1.1 nm after aging at 700 ◦C (Fig. 7 (b)).
The Cr element is significantly enriched at the grain boundary, while the Ni element is depleted at the corresponding position, suggesting the M23C6 phase, which is proved by the HRTEM (Fig. 8 (b)).
One M23C6 particle was found at the grain boundary triple junction (Fig. 9 (g ~ l)).
